messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher vitamin D levels were associated with lower BDI-II depression scores, with the association remaining after covariate adjustment.
Sentence: "A statistically significant negative association was identified for the BDI-II scale (B = -0.3170444, β = -0.2621328, p = 0.007) and the HAM-D17 scale (B = -0.1495026, β = -0.2829461, p = 0.002), which remained robust after adjustment for covariates (BDI-II: B = -0.2110473, β = -0.1744942, p = 0.050; HAMD17: B = -0.1153659, β = -0.2183397, p = 0.018)."
Measured as: depression severity (BDI-II)
Population: 90 adult inpatients with major depressive disorder in Romania
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower vitamin D levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 90
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a single-arm case series of a vitamin D3 plus folic acid and B12 combination in Parkinson's patients, with no comparator and a 15D dimension score; Study B is a cross-sectional association of serum vitamin D with BDI-II in depressed inpatients.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","intervention","outcome_measure","comparator"],"detail":"Parkinson's patients on levodopa vs inpatients with major depressive disorder; supplement combination vs measured serum level"}
